items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And Vaughn’s band had some good players in it, some real good soloists. We had a great lead alto player, Andy Bagni.

ctx.x: Almost like Paul Whiteman, they had some hot players mixed in there?

Yeah, well Paul was a little more I would say like symphony kind of thing, they were more classical end. And Vaughn’s band had some good players in it, some real good soloists. We had a great lead alto player, Andy Bagni. The band was built around what he did.
What was the work like at that time? Was it dances?

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So I graduated the week after, and I went on the road with Vaughn, and we played about ten weeks of theaters

ctx.x: Right. The transition from high school into Vaughn Monroe, we talked last time a little bit about him. And your parents were supportive of that?

Well they were in a way because my mother’s brothers were on the road — a brother was on the road — with a lot of different bands, Clyde McCoy, Buddy Rodgers, Raymond Scott, Teddy Powell, played with all the bands, played just rhythm but he was very good at it. Bob Chester. And I was on Christmas vacation, I was just about to graduate from my school and a lot of the big bands were losing men to the draft. And Vaughn Monroe almost gave up the band thinking that he was going to be drafted, but he didn’t. So he said…

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: I was finished with the big band. Vaughan broke up then.

ctx.x: I was finished with the big band. Vaughan broke up then. I went back to New York and luckily I got a job as a staff musician playing for the “Kate Smith Show.”
So what network was that on?
